facts.label: Pedir e passar comida
facts.sub: Peça com Can you pass the rice, please? ou Can I have some salt? Convide com Help yourself. Agradeça com This dinner is wonderful e Thank you for inviting me.

facts.label: Estilo família
facts.sub: Em jantares em casa, os pratos ficam no meio da mesa e cada um se serve. Peça para passar o que está longe com “Can you pass…?” e agradeça.

facts.label: Sal e pimenta
facts.sub: O sal e a pimenta estão quase sempre na mesa. “Pass the salt, please” é uma das frases mais comuns, e o costume é passar os dois juntos.

compare.br: In Brazil, people also share food, often put the dishes in the middle and say “pode se servir”.
compare.us: In the USA, “Help yourself” and “Pass the…” are common. Please and thank you are always used.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: People often pass dishes around the table.
You can grab food from across the table.
items.why: It is polite to ask someone to pass it.

items.s: “Help yourself” means take what you want.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.

answers: People often pass dishes around the table. → Verdadeiro (It is called family style.)
You can grab food from across the table. → Falso (It is polite to ask someone to pass it.)
“Help yourself” means take what you want. → Verdadeiro (It is a friendly invitation.)

“Dinner is ready. Please sit down.” says Kim. “Thank you. It smells great.” says Ali. “Help yourself to the chicken.” says Kim.
